policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads the singular, 'gainsaying of sinners against himself', and the mapped textual_variant note ('Many ancient authorities read themselves') puts the plural base reading in the margin, so r00 is excluded. The singular reflexive and the plain pronoun are indistinguishable in English, so r01 and r02 both stand.

ASV 'for what son is there whom his father chasteneth not?' supplies an English copula that any Greek nominal clause requires; it cannot show whether the Greek printed a copula. The only note is alternative_rendering ('Or, Endure unto chastening') and does not bear on this unit.
The candidates differ only in the position of the copula; 'then are ye bastards, and not sons' renders either order identically in English, and no note is mapped here.

ASV 'shall we not much rather be in subjection' renders the adverbial and the dative alike as 'much', and ASV routinely leaves a connective de untranslated, so the absence of an English conjunction excludes nothing. The verse note is alternative_rendering about 'our spirits'.

Neither particle is rendered at 'All chastening'; ASV's 'yet afterward' translates the later contrastive, which stands in every candidate. The English does not show whether the first particle was men or de.
Present and aorist imperative both give the ASV's 'make straight paths'; ASV does not mark imperative aspect. The note is alternative_rendering ('Or, put out of joint') and touches a different word.
ASV 'and thereby the many be defiled' renders either the pronoun or the demonstrative; 'thereby' distinguishes neither, and both verse notes are alternative_rendering on other words.
ASV reads 'thereby the many be defiled', with the definite 'the many' rather than 'many'. That definite rendering answers to the articular hoi polloi; the anarthrous reading would give simply 'many'.
ASV reads 'sold his own birthright'. The emphatic 'his own' renders the reflexive heautou; the plain pronoun autou would be rendered simply 'his'.

ASV 'come unto a mount that might be touched' names a mount, but 'a mount' is the kind of noun ASV supplies for a bare participle, and the verse's alternative rendering 'a palpable and kindled fire' construes the participles with 'fire' rather than with a mount. The English therefore does not settle whether the Greek printed the noun.
ASV 'unto blackness, and darkness' renders either gloom-word as 'darkness' after 'blackness'; the pair is not distinguished in English.

ASV 'entreated that no word more should be spoken unto them' takes its negative from the sense of the verb 'entreated (off)', which English supplies whether or not the redundant Greek negative stood in the text.
The candidates differ only in word order; 'who are enrolled in heaven' renders either arrangement identically.
ASV 'if they escaped not' renders the simple and the compound verb alike as 'escaped'; the compound's force is not marked in the English.
The candidates differ only in word order; 'when they refused him that warned them on earth' renders either arrangement identically.
ASV 'much more shall not we escape' renders the adverbial and the dative alike as 'much more'.
ASV reads 'Yet once more will I make to tremble not the earth only'. The future 'will I make to tremble' renders the future seiso; the present seio would be rendered 'I shake'.

The candidates differ in whether an article stands with 'removing' and where it falls. ASV 'signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken' supplies the English definite article as a matter of course for such a noun, so it shows neither the article's presence nor its position.

ASV reads 'let us have grace, whereby we may offer service well-pleasing to God'. 'We may offer service' continues the hortatory subjunctive of 'let us have'; the indicative latreuomen would be rendered 'whereby we serve'.

ASV reads 'with reverence and awe'. 'Awe' in second place renders deous; the alternative pairs aidous with eulabeias, which ASV renders as 'reverence'/'godly fear' (so the verse note, comparing 5:7) and would not yield 'awe' as the second term.
